140	
141	    from polymarket import AsyncPublicClient
142	    from polymarket.streams import CryptoPricesChainlinkTwapSpec
143	
144	
145	    async def main() -> None:
146	        async with AsyncPublicClient() as client:
147	            async with await client.subscribe(
148	                CryptoPricesChainlinkTwapSpec(
149	                    window_seconds=30,
150	                    symbols=["btc/usd"],
151	                )
152	            ) as stream:
153	                async for event in stream:
154	                    print(
155	                        event.payload.symbol,
156	                        event.payload.value,
157	                        event.payload.window_seconds,
158	                        event.payload.timestamp,
159	                    )
160	
161	
162	    asyncio.run(main())
163	    ```
164	
165	    Set `window_seconds` to `30` or `60`. Omit `symbols` to receive every
166	    available pair. The same subscription works with an `AsyncSecureClient`.
167	    Realtime subscriptions are not available on the synchronous clients.
168	
169	    <Accordion title="Example output">
170	      <CodeGroup>
171	        ```python CryptoPricesChainlinkTwapEvent Type theme={null}
172	        class CryptoPricesChainlinkTwapPayload:
173	            symbol: str
174	            timestamp: int
175	            value: Decimal
176	            window_seconds: Literal[30, 60]
177	
178	        class CryptoPricesChainlinkTwapEvent:
179	            topic: Literal["prices.crypto.chainlink.twap"]
180	            type: Literal["update"]
181	            timestamp: datetime | None
182	            payload: CryptoPricesChainlinkTwapPayload
183	        ```
184	
185	        ```json CryptoPricesChainlinkTwapEvent Example theme={null}
186	        {
187	          "topic": "prices.crypto.chainlink.twap",
188	          "type": "update",
189	          "timestamp": "2026-07-27T19:00:00.123000Z",
190	          "payload": {
191	            "symbol": "btc/usd",
192	            "timestamp": 1785178800000,
193	            "value": "65000.5",
194	            "window_seconds": 30
195	          }
196	        }
197	        ```
198	      </CodeGroup>
199	    </Accordion>
200	
201	    `payload.value` is an exact `Decimal` derived from Chainlink's fixed-point
202	    value. Use `payload.timestamp` as the Chainlink observation time; the outer
203	    `timestamp` is when the publisher submitted the update to RTDS.
204	
205	    The SDK restores the subscription after disconnects.
206	  </Tab>
207	
208	  <Tab title="API">
209	    Connect directly to RTDS when you need lower-level control:
210	
211	    ```text theme={null}
212	    wss://ws-live-data.polymarket.com
213	    ```
214	
215	    <Note>
216	      RTDS uses an application-level heartbeat. Send the text frame `PING` every 5
217	      seconds to maintain the connection.
218	    </Note>
219	
220	    Send a subscription frame for the lookback windows you need:
221	
222	    ```json theme={null}
223	    {
224	      "action": "subscribe",
225	      "subscriptions": [
226	        {
227	          "topic": "crypto_prices_twap_thirty",
228	          "type": "update",
229	          "filters": "{\"symbol\":\"btc/usd\"}"
230	        },
231	        {
232	          "topic": "crypto_prices_twap_sixty",
233	          "type": "update",
234	          "filters": "{\"symbol\":\"btc/usd\"}"
235	        }
236	      ]
237	    }
238	    ```
239	
240	    | Lookback window | RTDS topic                  |
241	    | --------------- | --------------------------- |
242	    | 30 seconds      | `crypto_prices_twap_thirty` |
243	    | 60 seconds      | `crypto_prices_twap_sixty`  |
244	
245	    `filters` must use the exact compact JSON form shown above, with one
246	    lowercase symbol and no spaces, such as `{"symbol":"btc/usd"}`. Omit it to
247	    receive every available symbol. If you need several symbols for one window,
248	    omit `filters` and filter updates by `payload.symbol` in your application.
249	
250	    <Accordion title="Example output">
251	      ```json theme={null}
252	      {
253	        "topic": "crypto_prices_twap_thirty",
254	        "type": "update",
255	        "timestamp": 1785178800123,
256	        "payload": {
257	          "symbol": "btc/usd",
258	          "value": 65000.5,
259	          "full_accuracy_value": "65000500000000000000000",
260	          "timestamp": 1785178800000,
261	          "window_s": 30
262	        }
263	      }
264	      ```
265	    </Accordion>
266	
267	    `full_accuracy_value` is the exact signed E18 fixed-point value. Divide it by
268	    10<sup>18</sup> with integer or decimal arithmetic. The numeric `value` is
269	    provided only for display convenience.
270	
271	    Use `payload.timestamp` as the Chainlink observation time; the outer
272	    `timestamp` is when the publisher submitted the update to RTDS. Direct
273	    clients must reconnect and resubscribe after a disconnect.
274	  </Tab>
275	</Tabs>
276	
277	### Select a Window
278	
279	Choose 30 or 60 seconds for each subscription. Subscribe twice for both.
280	
281	### Stream Behavior
282	
283	Subscriptions start with the next update. There is no snapshot, history, or
284	replay after a disconnect.
285	
286	## Use Chainlink Data Streams
287	
288	Use Chainlink Data Streams for direct mainnet access, the latest report before
289	streaming, or the original signed report. Find an asset's `TWAP: 30s` or `TWAP:
290	60s` ticker in the [Chainlink Data Streams
291	catalog](https://data.chain.link/streams), then copy its feed ID. Run this only
292	on a trusted backend; never expose Chainlink credentials to browsers or mobile
293	apps.
294	
295	<Steps>
296	  <Step title="Install and Connect">
297	    Use Node.js 20+ and TypeScript 5.3+. Install the Chainlink SDK:
298	
299	    ```bash theme={null}
300	    npm install --save-exact @chainlink/data-streams-sdk@1.2.1
301	    ```
302	
303	    Create the mainnet client:
304	
305	    ```ts theme={null}
306	    import {
307	      createClient,
308	      decodeReport,
309	      type Report,
310	    } from "@chainlink/data-streams-sdk";
311	
312	    type TwapFeed = {
313	      symbol: string;
314	      windowSeconds: 30 | 60;
315	    };
316	
317	    function requireEnv(name: string): string {
318	      const value = process.env[name];
319	
320	      if (!value) {
321	        throw new Error(`Missing required environment variable: ${name}`);
322	      }
323	
324	      return value;
325	    }
326	
327	    const client = createClient({
328	      apiKey: requireEnv("CHAINLINK_CLIENT_ID"),
329	      userSecret: requireEnv("CHAINLINK_CLIENT_SECRET"),
330	      endpoint: "https://api.dataengine.chain.link",
331	      wsEndpoint: "wss://ws.dataengine.chain.link",
332	      haMode: false,
333	    });
334	    ```
335	
336	    The SDK signs each request. Keep the server clock within five seconds of
337	    Chainlink's server time.
338	  </Step>
339	
340	  <Step title="Map and Decode Reports">
341	    Store the feed IDs from the catalog in server-side environment variables,
342	    then map each ID to its asset and window. Preserve the signed E18 price
343	    instead of converting it to a JavaScript `number`:
344	
345	    ```ts theme={null}
346	    const feeds = new Map<string, TwapFeed>([
347	      [
348	        requireEnv("CHAINLINK_TWAP_30S_FEED_ID").toLowerCase(),
349	        { symbol: "btc/usd", windowSeconds: 30 },
350	      ],
351	      [
352	        requireEnv("CHAINLINK_TWAP_60S_FEED_ID").toLowerCase(),
353	        { symbol: "btc/usd", windowSeconds: 60 },
354	      ],
355	    ]);
356	
357	    const E18 = 10n ** 18n;
358	
359	    function formatE18(value: bigint): string {
360	      const sign = value < 0n ? "-" : "";
361	      const absolute = value < 0n ? -value : value;
362	      const whole = absolute / E18;
363	      const fraction = (absolute % E18)
364	        .toString()
365	        .padStart(18, "0")
366	        .replace(/0+$/, "");
367	
368	      return `${sign}${whole}${fraction ? `.${fraction}` : ""}`;
369	    }
370	
371	    function readTwap(report: Report) {
372	      const feed = feeds.get(report.feedID.toLowerCase());
373	
374	      if (!feed) {
375	        throw new Error(`Unexpected Chainlink feed ID: ${report.feedID}`);
376	      }
377	
378	      const decoded = decodeReport(report.fullReport, report.feedID);
379	
380	      if (decoded.version !== "V2") {
381	        throw new Error(`Expected a V2 report, received ${decoded.version}`);
382	      }
383	
384	      return {
385	        feedID: report.feedID,
386	        symbol: feed.symbol,
387	        windowSeconds: feed.windowSeconds,
388	        value: formatE18(decoded.price),
389	        observedAt: new Date(report.observationsTimestamp * 1_000).toISOString(),
390	      };
391	    }
392	    ```
393	  </Step>
394	
395	  <Step title="Fetch Latest TWAP">
396	    Fetch each feed's latest report before streaming:
397	
398	    ```ts theme={null}
399	    const latestReports = await Promise.all(
400	      [...feeds.keys()].map((feedID) => client.getLatestReport(feedID)),
401	    );
402	
403	    for (const report of latestReports) {
404	      console.log(readTwap(report));
405	    }
406	    ```
407	
408	    <Accordion title="Output: Chainlink TWAP">
409	      ```json theme={null}
410	      {
411	        "feedID": "0x<mainnet-feed-id>",
412	        "symbol": "btc/usd",
413	        "windowSeconds": 30,
414	        "value": "65000.5",
415	        "observedAt": "2026-07-27T19:00:00.000Z"
416	      }
417	      ```
418	    </Accordion>
419	  </Step>
420	
421	  <Step title="Stream Updates">
422	    Subscribe to the selected feed IDs:
423	
424	    ```ts theme={null}
425	    const stream = client.createStream([...feeds.keys()]);
426	
427	    stream.on("report", (report) => {
428	      try {
429	        console.log(readTwap(report));
430	      } catch (error) {
431	        console.error("Failed to decode Chainlink report:", error);
432	      }
433	    });
434	
435	    stream.on("disconnected", () => {
436	      console.warn("Chainlink stream disconnected");
437	    });
438	
439	    stream.on("reconnecting", ({ attempt, delayMs }) => {
440	      console.warn(`Reconnecting: attempt ${attempt} in ${delayMs}ms`);
441	    });
442	
443	    stream.on("error", (error) => {
444	      console.error("Chainlink stream error:", error);
445	    });
446	
447	    await stream.connect();
448	
449	    process.once("SIGINT", async () => {
450	      await stream.close();
451	      process.exit(0);
452	    });
453	    ```
454	
455	    The SDK authenticates and reconnects automatically. Monitor `error`,
456	    `disconnected`, and `reconnecting`; restart the stream if retries are
457	    exhausted.
458	  </Step>
459	</Steps>
460	
461	### Read a Chainlink Report
462	
463	The TWAP feeds use Chainlink report schema V2. `decodeReport()` exposes the
464	encoded `benchmarkPrice` as `decoded.price`.
465	
466	| Value                          | How to use it                                                       |
467	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
468	| `report.feedID`                | Map the report to its asset and 30-second or 60-second window       |
469	| `decoded.price`                | Preserve the exact signed E18 value as a `bigint` or decimal string |
470	| `report.validFromTimestamp`    | Read the earliest valid time in Unix seconds                        |
471	| `report.observationsTimestamp` | Read the Chainlink observation time in Unix seconds                 |
472	| `decoded.expiresAt`            | Read the report expiration time in Unix seconds                     |
473	| `report.fullReport`            | Access the original signed Chainlink report                         |
474	
475	Reports do not include symbol or window labels. Maintain that mapping yourself,
476	never infer the window from update frequency, and use `observationsTimestamp`
477	for freshness checks.
478	
479	<Note>
480	  `decodeReport()` parses the report fields; it does not verify the DON
481	  signatures. Follow Chainlink's verification requirements before using a report
482	  for settlement or another trust-sensitive action.
483	</Note>
484	
485	### Find a Feed ID
486	
487	Open the [Chainlink Data Streams catalog](https://data.chain.link/streams) and
488	search for the asset and window you need, such as `BTC / USD - TWAP: 30s` or
489	`BTC / USD - TWAP: 60s`. Copy the feed ID from the product page and use it with
490	your existing standard or sponsored Data Streams credentials.
491	
492	| REST URL                            | WebSocket URL                    |
493	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
494	| `https://api.dataengine.chain.link` | `wss://ws.dataengine.chain.link` |
495	
496	The 30-second and 60-second values are lookback windows, not publication
497	cadences. Chainlink computes and signs the TWAP. Define a freshness threshold
498	and a fallback for report gaps instead of trying to infer the calculation from
499	the incoming updates. Chainlink does not currently publish the custom feed's
500	sampling boundaries, weighting, rounding, or missing-input behavior, so do not
501	independently reproduce the value without a specification from Chainlink.
502	
503	For production requirements, see Chainlink's [TypeScript SDK
504	reference](https://docs.chain.link/data-streams/reference/data-streams-api/ts-sdk),
505	[authentication
506	reference](https://docs.chain.link/data-streams/reference/data-streams-api/authentication),
507	and [developer
508	responsibilities](https://docs.chain.link/data-streams/developer-responsibilities).

2	> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.polymarket.com/llms.txt
3	> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
4	
5	# CLOB Trading Rate Limits
6	
7	> Per-signer token-bucket limits for CLOB order and cancellation requests
8	
9	Polymarket evaluates CLOB order and cancellation requests against separate token
10	buckets for each signer address. The signer address is the address associated
11	with your CLOB API credentials. Activity in one bucket does not consume capacity
12	from the other.
13	
14	<Warning>
15	  Beginning July 24, 2026, the limiter will run in warning mode for two weeks.
16	  Requests will continue to be processed during this period. A request that
17	  would be rejected after live enforcement begins will include
18	  `Poly-RateLimit-Warning: true`. Monitor this header and adjust your request
19	  patterns before live enforcement begins. Polymarket will announce when live
20	  enforcement begins.
21	</Warning>
22	
23	<Note>
24	  These per-signer limits are separate from the existing [Cloudflare IP-based
25	  limits](/api-reference/rate-limits), which remain unchanged.
26	</Note>
27	
28	## How Rate Limits Work
29	
30	Each signer has an order bucket and a cancel bucket:
31	
32	| Bucket | Request                        | Token Cost                                    |
33	| ------ | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
34	| Order  | `POST /order`                  | 1                                             |
35	| Order  | `POST /orders`                 | Number of orders in a non-empty batch         |
36	| Cancel | `DELETE /order`                | 1                                             |
37	| Cancel | `DELETE /orders`               | Number of submitted order IDs                 |
38	| Cancel | `DELETE /cancel-all`           | 1 plus the number of orders canceled          |
39	| Cancel | `DELETE /cancel-market-orders` | 1 plus the number of matching orders canceled |
40	
41	### Refill and Burst Capacity
42	
43	Tokens refill continuously at the rate assigned to the current tier. Burst
44	capacity is the maximum number of tokens a bucket can hold. A full bucket can
45	spend up to that capacity immediately; after the burst is consumed, new tokens
46	become available at the refill rate.
47	
48	Calculate the duration of a full burst as:
49	
50	```text theme={null}
51	burst_seconds = burst / rate_per_sec
52	```
53	
54	### Batch Requests
55	
56	Under live enforcement, a batch is admitted only when the bucket contains
57	enough tokens for every entry. Otherwise, the entire request is rejected and no
58	entries are processed. This all-or-nothing rule applies to the rate-limit check;
59	an admitted batch retains its normal per-order response behavior.
60	
61	A batch whose token cost exceeds the tier's burst capacity can never be admitted
62	as one request. Split it into smaller batches.
63	
64	### Cancel All and Cancel Market Orders
65	
66	The number of orders that will be canceled is not known when
67	`DELETE /cancel-all` or `DELETE /cancel-market-orders` begins. Each request
68	first consumes one cancel token. After the cancellation result is known, the
69	bucket is debited one additional token for every order successfully canceled.
70	
71	For tiers that allow a negative cancel balance, this second debit can put the
72	bucket into debt. Future cancel requests remain blocked until the bucket has
73	enough tokens for the next request. Other tiers floor the post-cancel balance at
74	zero regardless of debit size.
75	
76	## Volume Tiers
77	
78	Buckets are scoped to the signer address. Tier eligibility follows the
79	cumulative trading volume of the maker wallet, even when it differs from the
80	signer address. The volume window is currently 30 days, and tier assignments
81	refresh every three hours.
82	
83	| Tier     | 30-Day Volume | Order Rate (tokens/s) | Order Burst (tokens) | Cancel Rate (tokens/s) | Cancel Burst (tokens) | Negative Cancel Balance |
84	| -------- | ------------: | --------------------: | -------------------: | ---------------------: | --------------------: | :---------------------: |
85	| Standard |             — |                    40 |                   60 |                     80 |                   120 |           Yes           |
86	| Copper   |     \$30,000+ |                    60 |                   90 |                    120 |                   180 |           Yes           |
87	| Bronze   |     \$50,000+ |                    80 |                  120 |                    160 |                   240 |           Yes           |
88	| Silver   |    \$100,000+ |                   200 |                  300 |                    400 |                   600 |           Yes           |
89	| Gold     |    \$500,000+ |                   400 |                  600 |                    800 |                 1,200 |           Yes           |
90	| Platinum |       \$2.5M+ |                   450 |                  675 |                    900 |                 1,350 |            No           |
91	| Diamond  |         \$5M+ |                   525 |                  787 |                  1,050 |                 1,575 |            No           |
92	| Elite    |        \$10M+ |                   600 |                  900 |                  1,200 |                 1,800 |            No           |
93	
94	Tier thresholds, the volume window, and rate limits may change as the system is
95	tuned. Polymarket will provide advance notice of significant changes.
96	
97	## Response Headers
98	
99	Responses include the following headers when the limiter successfully evaluates
100	a covered request:
101	
102	| Header                     | Description                                                                 |
103	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
104	| `Poly-RateLimit-Remaining` | Current token balance for the applicable bucket after rate-limit accounting |
105	| `Poly-RateLimit-Reset`     | Unix timestamp when the current rate-limit wait period ends                 |
106	| `Poly-RateLimit-Tier`      | Rate-limit tier applied to the request                                      |
107	
108	The following headers appear only in specific cases:
109	
110	| Header                   | Description                                                                  |
111	| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
112	| `Retry-After`            | Retry delay in seconds; included on `429` responses                          |
113	| `Poly-RateLimit-Warning` | `true` in warning mode when live enforcement would have rejected the request |
114	
115	`Poly-RateLimit-Reset` is not the time when the bucket will be completely full.
116	On a `429` response for a request whose token cost fits within burst capacity,
117	it indicates when enough tokens are expected for the attempted request. On an
118	admitted request, it may be the current timestamp.
119	
120	`Poly-RateLimit-Remaining` can be negative after `DELETE /cancel-all` or
121	`DELETE /cancel-market-orders` for tiers that allow a negative cancel balance.
122	Before sending a large batch, compare its token cost with the remaining balance.
123	
124	## Handle 429 Responses
125	
126	After live enforcement begins, a request that requires more tokens than the
127	applicable bucket contains returns `429 Too Many Requests`.
128	
129	For a request whose token cost is within the tier's burst capacity,
130	`Retry-After` gives the minimum delay before retrying. You do not need to wait
131	for the bucket to refill completely. If the request costs more than the burst
132	capacity, split it into smaller requests instead of retrying it unchanged.
133	
134	## Get Help
135	
136	Contact [support@polymarket.com](mailto:support@polymarket.com) if you have
137	questions about your tier, believe your wallet qualifies for a higher tier,
138	recently moved trading activity to a new address, or believe you are being
139	limited incorrectly.
